description.text: The DNA Methyltransferase 3 family is involved in the process of adding methyl groups to the 5 position of cytosine in DNA, a key epigenetic modification essential for development and gene regulation. Members of the family are responsible for de novo methylation, establishing DNA methylation patterns, and are linked to the methylation of histones, suggesting a coordinated regulation of epigenetic marks. Some members preferentially methylate DNA at nucleosomal cores or linkers and may also methylate non-CpG sites. The family includes catalytically active enzymes that can repress transcription by recruiting HDAC activity, and catalytically inactive regulatory factors that modulate the activity of active members. These proteins play roles in imprinting, gene silencing, retrotransposon repression in germ cells, and RNA-directed DNA methylation, with implications in plant and animal development.

description.text: The C5-methyltransferase family is comprised of enzymes that primarily methylate cytosine residues within specific DNA sequences, playing a crucial role in the regulation of gene expression, maintenance of DNA methylation patterns, and protection of DNA from endonuclease cleavage. Members of this family recognize various DNA motifs, often methylating the cytosine at the 5' position. Some members preferentially methylate hemimethylated DNA, contributing to epigenetic inheritance by preserving methylation patterns during DNA replication and cell division. Others are part of restriction-modification systems, protecting bacterial genomes from phage infections by methylating specific sequences and thereby preventing cleavage by corresponding restriction endonucleases. This family also includes enzymes involved in the defense against phages through systems like DISARM. In plants, these methyltransferases are involved in genomic imprinting, embryogenesis, and seed viability, often targeting CHG and CpG sites for methylation, which is essential for gene silencing and suppression of transposable elements.

ec.description: ENZYME is a repository of information relative to the nomenclature of enzymes. It is primarily based on the recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) and it describes each type of characterized enzyme for which an EC (Enzyme Commission) number has been provided.
